title: China's Politburo Pledges Targeted Stimulus, Faster Fiscal Spending — Stops Short of Major Easing
detail: China's Politburo, meeting July 30-31 in Beijing under the Communist Party leadership, struck a more supportive tone on the economy following Q2 GDP's slowdown to 4.3%, pledging to roll out 'pragmatic and effective new policies in a timely manner,' step up counter-cyclical adjustment, and accelerate fiscal spending — but announced no large-scale stimulus package. Economists characterized the readout as broadly in line with expectations, emphasizing better use of already-approved measures over a dramatic new easing push, disappointing investors hoping for a bigger policy signal after the growth miss.

title: Eurozone July Inflation Rises to 2.9% as Energy Costs Climb on Middle East Tensions
detail: Eurostat's flash estimate showed eurozone annual inflation rising to 2.9% in July from 2.8% in June, with core inflation (ex-food and energy) ticking up to 2.5% from 2.4%. Energy prices posted the highest annual rate of any component at 10.0%, followed by services at 3.3%, as the July 23 Red Sea/Hormuz oil shock pushed crude and fuel costs higher across the bloc. Inflation ranged widely by member state, from 2.0% in Estonia to 5.6% in Lithuania.
